methodology: The study involved the synthesis of maleimide-terminated oligoimides with controlled molar mass for polymerization, followed by thermal radical polymerization to induce cross-linking in the polyimide matrix. The microstructures were optionally regulated through copolymerization with styrene.
research_objective: To develop a low dielectric constant and high-performance dielectric material suitable for next-generation high-frequency applications, such as internet-of-things (IoTs) and high-speed data communications.

key_findings.finding: The synthesis of low dielectric constant polyimide via chemical cross-linking of maleimide-terminated oligoimides results in a material with improved dielectric properties (Dk =2.78, Df =0.0042 @28 GHz) and enhanced mechanical integrity compared to linear PI.
Polyimide materials exhibit excellent dielectric stability and robustness over a wide range of environments.
The use of end-functionalized polymer chains enables the orthogonal design with low Dk values in the range of 3.0-3.6 at high frequency regime.
Synthesis of maleimide-terminated oligoimides by linking 4,4′-Isopropylidenediphenoxy)diphthalic anhydride (BPADA) and 2,2-Bis [4-(4-aminophenoxy)phenyl] propane (BAPP).
Optimization of cross-linking density to achieve low dielectric properties without compromising structural robustness.
Dielectric performance of the BMI films can be systematically evaluated by varying chain length and introducing styrene comonomer to PI-BPADA- BAPPs
Density measurement and WAXS confirm the generation of free volume in the polymer network

The tendency of film density depending on the molar mass of the oligomer suggests that the modu- lation of free volume is achieved by controlling the number of cross- linking junctions. Also, the incorporation of a molecular spacer pro- vides further modulation of free volumes by expanding inter-maleimide distances via alternating copolymerization between styrene and mal- eimide. This change in film density indicates the formation of perma- nently trapped free volume, offering controllable parameters for adjusting free spaces within the polymer matrix.
